bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470093 (harfbuzz): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target hb-subset-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470093
bug_description.normalized: In vulnerable commit `a26806801005c28115ae9e48bdcf3bbbc1bcd767`, hb-subset-fuzzer loads a malformed GSUB table whose only lookup is a LigatureSubst format-1 subtable with `coverage = 0x001c` landing on the final two bytes of the sanitized 164-byte GSUB blob. `Coverage::sanitize()` accepts that blob-end stub because unknown coverage formats fall through `default:return true`. Later `OT::LigatureSubstFormat1::closure` constructs `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (this+coverage)`, and the generic `hb_auto_t (T1 t1)` constructor copies the short `Coverage` object by value. That implicit fixed-size copy reads past the end of the 164-byte heap allocation before `Coverage::Iter` can examine the invalid format, producing the observed AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow at `src/hb-ot-layout-gsub-table.hh:778`. Commit `2dde6c803a9e50c5bff74095187b0cb2e12eebdd` fixes the bug by removing the catch-all by-value constructor and allowing only pointer/reference construction.

source.description: The first vulnerability-relevant read on the crashing path resolves the attacker-controlled ligature-subtable `coverage` offset into the specific `Coverage` object later copied out of bounds.
source.value_from: The staged 2648-byte witness advertises a `GSUB` table at file offset 2484. After `hb_blob_create_sub_blob()` clamps the bogus table length to EOF and sanitization makes that slice writable, the GSUB blob is 164 bytes long. Inside it, lookup 0 is a type-4 lookup whose format-1 ligature subtable starts at `GSUB+0x86` and stores `coverage = 0x001c`, so this read materializes `obj` at `GSUB+0xa2`, the final two bytes `0x20 0x20` of the heap blob.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable helper takes the font-backed `Coverage` object by value as ctor-local `t1` instead of by reference, so constructing `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` copies the short blob-end object past the heap extent that sanitization allocated for the GSUB table.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. Constructing local `iter` from `this+coverage` triggers the by-value `hb_auto_t` constructor and overreads the 164-byte sanitized GSUB heap blob by 5 bytes.

parser_admitted.description: On the witnessed subset path, `drop_ot_layout` is false, so `_populate_gids_to_retain()` calls `_gsub_closure()` and dispatches attacker-controlled GSUB lookups.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the exact font-backed `Coverage` object that later gets copied out of bounds. Its base is derived from the ligature-subtable `coverage` field `0x001c`, and in the witnessed blob it consists only of the terminal bytes `0x20 0x20`.

coarse_trace.summary: GSUB sanitization duplicates the selected table into a 164-byte writable heap blob, creating the extent that the later constructor copy overreads.
The ligature subtable's `coverage` offset resolves to a 2-byte invalid-format stub at the end of the GSUB blob, and `Coverage::sanitize()` accepts it through the default branch.
Lookup 0 dispatches its format-1 ligature-substitution subtable, making `OT::LigatureSubstFormat1::closure` reachable on the crashing path.
Constructing `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` from `this+coverage` routes through the by-value `hb_auto_t` constructor and immediately overreads the blob-end `Coverage` object.

fine_trace.note: During `sanitize_blob<OT::GSUB>()`, HarfBuzz makes the selected GSUB table writable. In the staged 2648-byte witness, the sfnt directory advertises a `GSUB` record at file offset 2484 with bogus length `0x20202020`; `hb_blob_create_sub_blob()` clamps that to EOF, so `this->length` is 164 and this allocation creates the exact heap region later reported by ASan.

The ligature-substitution format-1 header in the sanitized GSUB blob stores `coverage = 0x001c`. Applying that offset to subtable base `GSUB+0x86` materializes `obj` at `GSUB+0xa2`, the final two bytes of the 164-byte heap blob; those bytes are `0x20 0x20` and no Coverage body remains after them.

`Coverage::sanitize()` first checks only the 2-byte format field. With `u.format == 0x2020`, it takes the default branch and accepts this end-of-blob Coverage stub without requiring a `CoverageFormat1` or `CoverageFormat2` body, so the malformed offset survives sanitization.

When subset closure later visits lookup 0, the lookup's only type-4 subtable has `u.format == 1`, so dispatch enters `LigatureSubstFormat1::closure`. That makes the same `coverage = 0x001c` field in this subtable relevant on the crashing path.

On the reached format-1 closure path, `this+coverage` resolves the same attacker-controlled `coverage = 0x001c` field again. The constructor argument is therefore the same 2-byte Coverage stub at `GSUB+0xa2`, and local iterator `iter` is about to be initialized from that blob-end object.

The helper takes the Coverage object by value as ctor-local `t1` instead of by reference. For this sample, the resolved Coverage object has only the final two valid bytes of the 164-byte blob, so the implicit C++ copy of `t1` reads past the end of that heap buffer before `Coverage::Iter` can examine the invalid format. The fix removes this catch-all overload and keeps only pointer/reference construction.

AddressSanitizer sink. Instantiating `iter` at this call site triggers the by-value copy from step 5, and ASan reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` here at address `0x60f0000001d9`, which is 5 bytes past the 164-byte heap allocation from step 0.

format.name: sfnt-like font with terminal GSUB Coverage stub
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 2648-byte witness stored in `poc`. It begins `00 01 00 00`, advertises 32 table-directory entries, and its third directory slot is tag `GSUB` with `offset = 2484` and `length = 0x20202020`; `hb_blob_create_sub_blob()` therefore clamps the selected GSUB slice to the final 164 bytes of the file. Inside that slice, the lookup list has one lookup, lookup 0 is type 4 with a format-1 ligature subtable at `GSUB+0x86`, and that subtable's `coverage` field is `0x001c`, landing on the final two bytes `0x20 0x20` of the slice. That exact layout makes `Coverage::sanitize()` accept the stub via its default branch and then drives `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (this+coverage)` into the by-value `hb_auto_t` constructor, which overreads the 164-byte writable GSUB blob.
